title: Pipkin Finds the Moonpetal
markdown:
Rowan Cloud skipped along the sleepy cedar trail. Her hair swirled like soft mist. Her little boots made soft thuds on the mossy path.

“Rupert!” she called. Her voice sounded like tiny bells.

Rupert Bells trotted up beside her. His eyes were kind and sparkly, like smooth river pebbles.

“The moonpetal is lost!” Rowan said. Her smile was wide. She was excited. “We must find it before the big moon peeks over the hills!”

Rupert chuckled. His smile was warm. “A moonpetal race! That sounds like fun, Rowan. But where do you think it went?”

Just then, a tiny white blur zipped past their feet. It was Pipkin, a snow-white mouse. His nose twitched. His whiskers wiggled. Pipkin loved adventures with Rowan and Rupert.

“Hmm,” said Rowan. She tapped her chin. She thought hard. “I think it might have tumbled into a big nodding bell-flower near the cave that glows!” She pointed her finger. A soft shimmery light peeked out from behind the trees.

“That’s a nice idea, Rowan,” said Rupert. He tilted his head. “But I was thinking it might have floated near the pretty lantern bridge. The one that looks like sleepy stars over the brook?” He pointed the other way. Soft lanterns were starting to twinkle.

“Hooray!” said Rowan. She clapped her hands. They made a happy sound. “Two good ideas! Let’s look in our own special places.”

Rowan skipped toward the glowing cave. The air felt soft and warm. It smelled like sweet dew after a gentle rain. She peeked into a big purple bell-flower. Inside, she found a perfectly round shiny dewdrop. It sparkled like a tiny diamond. But it was not the moonpetal.

Rupert walked toward the lantern bridge. His footsteps made a soft crunching sound. The lanterns glowed with a gentle warm light. He looked under the bridge and around the mossy stones. He found a fluffy dandelion puff. It looked ready to fly. But still, no moonpetal.

Little Pipkin darted playfully between Rowan and Rupert. His nose twitched. His whiskers wiggled. He did not go to the cave. He did not go to the bridge. He went to a green fern in the middle, where the two paths almost touched.

Pipkin squeaked a tiny happy squeak. He nudged something small and shimmering on the fern.

Rowan and Rupert met in the middle. They both had smiles, but no moonpetal.

“I found a dewdrop,” said Rowan. She held it out. It still sparkled.

“And I found a dandelion puff,” said Rupert. He held it carefully.

They both looked down. There, sparkling on the soft green moss, was the little shimmering petal Pipkin had nudged. It glowed with a soft gentle light.

“The moonpetal!” they both said. Happy surprise bubbled up. They giggled.

“Oh, Pipkin!” said Rowan. She gently scooped up the tiny mouse. She gave him a warm hug. “You found it for us! You’re the best finder ever!”

Rupert smiled. His eyes twinkled. He did not say who had looked in the better place. He only looked at the fern, and at Pipkin’s whiskers, still wiggling.

Just then, the big sleepy moon began to peek over the mountains. It cast a soft gentle glow on the trail. Rowan and Rupert walked hand-in-hand. Pipkin nestled happily in Rowan’s pocket. The lost moonpetal was safe between them. The dewdrop and the dandelion puff came too, because they had been found as well.
characters: Pipkin (snow-white mouse), Rowan Cloud (mist-haired young witch)
audience: children aged 3-4, story time at home
author: StoryGen Community
